name: Avatar
description: Compact secondary identity cue using supplied initials or a neutral fallback. Avatar does not infer identity, status, role, presence, verification, or interaction behavior.

props.name: initials
props.description: Optional consumer-supplied short initials. Avatar never derives initials from a name, email, or other identity data.

props.name: size
props.description: Governed Avatar geometry. sm is 32 CSS pixels and lg is 48 CSS pixels.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Optional native accessible label for a standalone meaningful identity visual. When omitted, Avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

representations.mapsTo: initials when non-empty initials are supplied; fallback otherwise
decorative aria-hidden semantics by default; role=img plus aria-label when labeled

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Circular 32px or 48px semantic-token surface with centered identity cue.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.description: Consumer-supplied initials or the governed neutral fallback character @.

semantics.accessibleName: By default the Avatar is decorative because adjacent visible identity text should own the person's accessible identity. A supplied aria-label makes a standalone Avatar image-like and names it explicitly.
semantics.focus: Avatar is non-interactive and does not create or move focus.
requirements: When aria-label is omitted or empty, Avatar renders aria-hidden=true and does not expose decorative initials or fallback content to assistive technology.
When a non-empty aria-label is supplied, Avatar exposes image-like role=img semantics and uses that aria-label as its accessible name.
Avatar never infers initials from a name, email, gender, or any other personal attribute; product code supplies initials explicitly.
When initials are absent or whitespace-only, content is derived as the governed neutral @ fallback.
size=sm is exactly 32 by 32 CSS pixels and size=lg is exactly 48 by 48 CSS pixels.
The initials/fallback typography uses the label/small semantic typography and remains centered in both LTR and RTL contexts.
No photo, presence, status, role, verified, selected-person, or clickable account-menu variant exists in version 1.0.0.
